frameworks.name: HR / Recruiter Screen
frameworks.purpose: Filter for baseline fit: compensation, logistics, motivation, communication skills
typical_questions: Tell me about yourself
Why are you interested in this role?
Why are you leaving your current role?
What are your salary expectations?
What's your notice period / availability?
What do you know about our company?
Where do you see yourself in 5 years?
What's your ideal work environment?
preparation_focus: 90-second pitch tailored to the role
Clear, honest reason for leaving
Salary range researched and ready
2-3 sentences about the company showing genuine knowledge
Enthusiasm without desperation
red_flags_to_avoid: Badmouthing previous employer
Vague or generic answers about the company
Salary expectations wildly misaligned
Lack of questions about the role
questions_to_ask: What does the interview process look like from here?
What's the team structure for this role?
What does success look like in the first 6 months?
Is there anything about my background you'd like me to clarify?

frameworks.name: Hiring Manager Interview
frameworks.purpose: Assess technical competence, team fit, and ability to deliver in the specific role
typical_questions: Tell me about yourself
Walk me through your most impactful project
How do you approach [core responsibility of the role]?
Tell me about a time you dealt with a difficult stakeholder
Describe a time something went wrong and how you handled it
How do you prioritise competing demands?
What's your approach to [specific technology/methodology]?
Why this company? Why this team?
Where do you need to grow?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision
preparation_focus: Deep understanding of the JD requirements
4-6 STAR stories covering leadership, technical delivery, stakeholder management, failure/recovery
Specific examples mapped to each JD requirement
Understanding of the team's current challenges
Genuine questions showing you've thought about the role
red_flags_to_avoid: Generic answers not specific to the role
Inability to go deep on claimed experience
No questions about the team or challenges
Arrogance or inability to acknowledge growth areas
questions_to_ask: What's the biggest challenge the team is facing right now?
How do you measure success for this role?
What does the team's roadmap look like for the next 6-12 months?
What's the working style of the team — how do you collaborate?
What would make someone really successful vs. just adequate in this role?

frameworks.name: Culture / Values Interview
frameworks.purpose: Assess alignment with company values, collaboration style, and cultural add
typical_questions: Tell me about a time you went above and beyond
How do you handle conflict with a colleague?
Describe your ideal team environment
Tell me about a time you received difficult feedback
How do you handle ambiguity?
What motivates you?
Tell me about a time you helped someone on your team
How do you handle work-life balance?
preparation_focus: Research company values and map stories to each value
Authentic examples — interviewers detect rehearsed answers
Emphasis on collaboration, growth mindset, and self-awareness
Specific examples of helping others, receiving feedback, and adapting
red_flags_to_avoid: Taking sole credit for team achievements
Inability to describe personal growth or learning
Generic, values-poster answers
Negativity about previous teams or companies
questions_to_ask: How would you describe the team culture?
What do people enjoy most about working here?
How does the team handle disagreements?
What's the onboarding experience like?

frameworks.name: Technical Interview — Data / Analytics
frameworks.purpose: Assess hands-on technical skills in SQL, Python, data modelling, and domain-specific knowledge
typical_questions: Write a SQL query to [specific scenario]
How would you design a data model for [domain]?
Walk me through how you'd build a data pipeline for [use case]
How do you handle data quality issues?
Explain your approach to query optimisation
What's the difference between [technical concept A] and [technical concept B]?
How do you handle slowly changing dimensions?
Describe your experience with [specific tool/platform from JD]
How would you reconcile data from two different sources?
Walk me through a technical architecture you designed
preparation_focus: SQL fluency — joins, window functions, CTEs, aggregation, subqueries
Data modelling concepts — star schema, normalisation, SCDs
Python data processing — Pandas, data pipelines, API integration
Query optimisation — execution plans, indexing, partitioning
Domain-specific data knowledge (investment data if finance role)
Whiteboard/verbal explanation of architecture decisions
red_flags_to_avoid: Unable to write basic SQL
No understanding of data modelling
Can't explain architecture decisions and trade-offs
Overcomplicating simple problems
questions_to_ask: What does the tech stack look like?
What's the most challenging data problem the team is working on?
How is data quality monitored and maintained?
What does the development workflow look like — version control, code review, deployment?

frameworks.name: Technical Interview — Software Engineering
frameworks.purpose: Assess coding ability, system design, and engineering best practices
typical_questions: Solve this coding problem [algorithm/data structure]
Design a system that [high-level requirement]
How would you scale [existing system] to handle 10x traffic?
Walk me through your testing approach
How do you handle errors and edge cases?
Explain the architecture of something you built
What's your approach to code review?
How do you decide between [framework A] and [framework B]?
preparation_focus: LeetCode medium-level problems (arrays, strings, hashmaps, trees)
System design fundamentals — load balancing, caching, databases, queues
Be able to discuss projects in deep technical detail
Testing strategies — unit, integration, E2E
Clean code principles and trade-offs
red_flags_to_avoid: Can't code a basic algorithm
No consideration of edge cases
Can't explain trade-offs in design decisions
No experience with testing or version control
questions_to_ask: What's the engineering culture like — how opinionated is the team?
What does the deployment process look like?
How do you handle technical debt?
What's the most interesting technical challenge the team has solved recently?

frameworks.name: Case Study / Presentation
frameworks.purpose: Assess structured thinking, communication, and ability to solve open-ended problems
frameworks.typical_format: Given a business problem or dataset, prepare an analysis/recommendation and present it. May be given in advance (take-home) or on the spot.
typical_questions: Here's a dataset — what insights can you find?
A stakeholder wants X — how would you approach it?
Walk us through your analysis methodology
What assumptions did you make and why?
How would you present these findings to a non-technical audience?
What would you do differently with more time?
preparation_focus: Structured problem-solving framework (define → analyse → recommend → validate)
Clear, concise presentation skills
Ability to handle ambiguity and state assumptions explicitly
Data visualisation best practices
Anticipate follow-up questions and have answers ready
red_flags_to_avoid: Jumping to solutions without defining the problem
Poor presentation skills or unclear communication
Inability to handle pushback on assumptions
Overcomplicating the analysis
questions_to_ask: How often does the team work on this type of analysis?
Who are the typical stakeholders for this kind of work?
How do you balance speed vs. rigour in analysis?
